Lemma
[Regularity of the distance function] 1. ch14:14.16\group ch14-boundary-gradient Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0367 Let $\Omega $ be bounded and $\partial \Omega \in C^k$, $k\geq 2$. There is $\mu >0$, depending on $\Omega $, such that $d\in C^k(\Gamma _\mu )$, where $\Gamma _\mu =\{ x\in \Omega :d(x)<\mu \} $.
Proof

\sketch Choose $\mu $ below the uniform interior normal radius. Every $x\in \Gamma _\mu $ has a unique nearest boundary point $y(x)$ and

egin{equation} x=y+ u (y)d. ag {14.96} \end{equation}

In principal coordinates the normal map $(y',d)\mapsto y+ u (y)d$ has

egin{equation} D\mathbf g=\diag (1-\kappa _1d,\ldots ,1-\kappa _{n-1}d,1) ag {14.97} \end{equation}

and

egin{equation} \det D\mathbf g=\prod _{i=1}^{n-1}(1-\kappa _id)>0. ag {14.98} \end{equation}

The inverse function theorem makes $y$ and $d$ smooth; since $Dd= u (y(x))$, one gains the final derivative and obtains $d\in C^k$.

□
